summary: On node1 (RHEL 9.8), configured /etc/security/pwquality.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3 so new user passwords must be at least 12 characters and use at least 3 distinct character classes. PAM already invoked pam_pwquality.so via authselect's system-auth/password-auth (requisite), so no PAM stack changes were needed. Verified enforcement as a non-root user (root bypasses pwquality by default, so tests were run via sudo -u testuser passwd): a sub-12-char password was rejected, a 12+ char password with only 2 classes was rejected, and a 12+ char 3-class password was accepted. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and config state, rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified the pwquality config, PAM hooks, and live password enforcement post-reboot with a fresh test user, then cleaned up all test users.
actions_performed: Captured baseline boot_id and pre-existing pwquality/PAM state on node1
Backed up /etc/security/pwquality.conf and set minlen=12, minclass=3
Confirmed pam_pwquality.so already wired into system-auth and password-auth via requisite
Validated enforcement as a non-root user: short password rejected, 2-class password rejected, compliant 12-char/3-class password accepted
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until exec was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed after reboot, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified pwquality.conf settings, PAM hooks, and enforcement behavior post-reboot
Cleaned up all temporary test users

evidence.requirement: Baseline health/state captured before any changes
evidence.summary: Captured initial boot_id, OS version, and confirmed pam_pwquality.so exists and is already invoked by system-auth/password-auth, with no active pwquality.conf directives yet.

evidence.requirement: Password policy configured: min length 12, min 3 character classes
evidence.summary: Set minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf and confirmed the values are present in the file.

evidence.requirement: Policy actually enforced for new user passwords
evidence.summary: As a non-root user, a less-than-12-char password was rejected, a 12+ char password with only 2 character classes was rejected, and a 12+ char password with 3 classes was accepted.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline for node1 before mandatory restart
evidence.summary: Recorded pre-restart boot_id and confirmed pwquality.conf and PAM hooks were in the desired state immediately before reboot.
Triggered systemctl reboot in the background; the exec call returned before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart, then changed boot identity proving restart occurred
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeout/reset while node1 was rebooting, then a successful connection returning a new boot_id differing from the pre-restart value, proving an actual reboot.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required configuration and enforcement behavior
evidence.summary: After reboot, pwquality.conf still shows minlen=12/minclass=3, PAM hooks still reference pam_pwquality.so, and live enforcement re-tested as a non-root user again shows short password rejected, 2-class password rejected, and compliant password accepted.
